analysis:
This batch holds only documentation and a changelog; no executable source was supplied. The Swift implementations named in the docs (ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift, PromptTokenCache.swift, tokenizer and template-loop changes) are outside the evidence, so I cannot judge their security.

Changes described:
(1) A per-scope prompt piece-token cache keeps token IDs for chat-template pieces. It is capped at DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE_MB, default 32 MiB per tokenizer, as ordinary heap. Per the changelog it is keyed by the "same prefix-cache scope", which is coordinator-authored per account, model and prompt contract (T-041, A-001). If the implementation keys on scope correctly, there is no new cross-tenant disclosure. If the scope were omitted, it could create a cross-tenant timing or token-reuse channel, since prompt preparation time drops from about 100-260 ms to 5-8 ms on a hit. This is the same-account TTFT oracle that SEC-035 already accepts, but the cross-scope isolation of the new store should be checked in code. The cache holds token IDs of decrypted prompt text in process memory only, which stays inside the TB-003 and TB-007 plaintext boundary, but it extends A-001 retention. Whether it is cleared on tokenizer unload or model eviction is unverified.
(2) Templates for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS get linear-time equivalents of their loops. Equivalence is self-checked at load and sampled in the background, with a kill switch. A divergence in tokenization would affect prompt correctness and billing counts, not confidentiality.
(3) The work-FIFO consumer is released while a cold model load waits (releaseWorkFIFO). Docs say attestation challenges and cancels proceed, and cancels are applied on admission return. This reinforces the availability goal in TB-011 and T-057. Connection, drain and model-management events still wait. The relevant race is with admission and memory accounting (hardware-support.md lines 318-340): a resident-model request can take a slot the released load would have evicted, so the load later fails at the post-acceptance gate. This is availability only, and the documented gate, pending-load claims and eviction still decide loads. Concurrent overtaking could affect T-053 stale-authorization ordering; the code needs to confirm that grant and connection-invalidation checks are still applied at request selection and execution.
(4) The decrypted request body is parsed once instead of five times, which reduces the plaintext handling surface.

No regression identified from the docs alone. Integration should review the implementation for cache-scope keying, memory bounds, cancel handling during a released load, and ordering with connection invalidation.
